claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 12 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 12 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the children you're claiming for.

**How old is your child (or children)?** 

Please let me know:
- The name(s) of your child/children
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age category:
- **Under 16**: Automatic qualification (if other requirements are met)
- **16-19**: Need to check if they're in full-time education or approved training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I'm eligible for Child Benefit.

I have one child - Alex, who is 12 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, **Alex, who is 12 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, that's a great starting point as this category has automatic qualification potential. However, I need to check a few more things to confirm eligibility.

Let me ask the next question:

**Is Alex working full-time (30 hours or more per week)?**

This is important because even though Alex is under 16, if they're in full-time work, they wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not working in paid work at all?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's only 12, so he's still in school full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's helpful to know. Since Alex doesn't work and is in full-time school, that's a positive sign. Let me continue checking the eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Most 12-year-olds won't be, but I need to confirm this for the assessment)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own right. He's just a regular 12-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's exactly what we'd expect. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 12 and in full-time school, I'm expecting the answer is no, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just at regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Now let me move forward with checking the residency requirements, which is an important part of the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. There are several paths that can qualify you, so let me ask:

**Which of the following best describes your situation:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (most common case)
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and are working, jobseeking, studying, have sufficient resources, or are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Which category applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward. Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue with the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. Responsibility can be shown in different ways:

**Which of these applies to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** (most common case)
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - This means you pay towards their care (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc.) at least the equivalent of Child Benefit
3. **You pay maintenance payments** under a court order or agreement that covers Alex's upkeep

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That confirms you're responsible for Alex. Let me continue with the next checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim Child Benefit for him?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another relative
- Someone else with responsibility for Alex

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me check Alex's living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living:**

1. **At home with you** (normal living situation)
2. **In hospital** (long-term)
3. **In local authority care**
4. **Fostered** (with another family)

Which describes Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is at home with me - just a normal living situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what we'd expect. Let me continue with the final checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is Alex's care and living costs fully your responsibility (not subsidised by the council)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. I'm responsible for all of Alex's care and living costs. The council isn't paying anything towards him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's all the information I need. Based on your answers, I can now provide you with a final decision on your Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I can now provide you with your eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

Congratulations! Based on your circumstances, **you qualify for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why You're Eligible:

✓ **Alex is 12 years old** (under 16 - automatic qualification)
✓ **Alex is not in full-time paid work** (still in school)
✓ **Alex is not receiving benefits** in his own right
✓ **Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship**
✓ **You're a UK resident** (living in Manchester)
✓ **You're responsible for Alex** (living with you full-time)
✓ **No one else is claiming** for Alex
✓ **Alex is living at home normally** (not in hospital or care)
✓ **You're fully responsible for his care** (council not paying)

### What You Need to Do Next:

1. **Apply for Child Benefit** - You can:
   - Apply online at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
   - Or apply by post using form CH2

2. **Prepare these documents:**
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your address (utility bill, council tax band, etc.)

3. **Important Note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or a partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which recovers some of the benefit through tax
   - This doesn't make you ineligible, but you should be aware of it

4. **Payment Schedule:**
   - Payments are usually made every 4 weeks directly into your bank account
   - Single parents or those receiving certain benefits may receive weekly payments

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?
